newsitem.title: INDIA: Sikh party to take charge in India's Punjab state.
newsitem.headline: Sikh party to take charge in India's Punjab state.

text.p: A pro-Sikh party was due to take office in India's northern state of Punjab on Wednesday after it handed the Congress party its worst defeat in local elections last week.

The Akali Dal party of former state chief minister Prakash Singh Badal and its Hindu nationalist ally, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), won a four-fifths majority in Friday's polls for the 117-member assembly.
The key local polls were the first in two decades not overshadowed by violence stemming from a Sikh separatist revolt. More than 20,000 people were killed in insurgency-related violence.
"We will give the people of Punjab an honest and transparent government," Badal told Reuters on Tuesday.
He said his government would be sworn in at a sprawling sports stadium instead of the traditional ceremony at the state governor's residence.
"We want the people of Punjab to rejoice in this historic victory," Badal said.
Congress won only 14 seats, a sharp reversal from the 87 seats it held in the last assembly.
The Akali Dal party won 74 seats, and its ally in the state, the BJP, won 18.
An independent survey showed Congress garnered only 27 percent of votes in Punjab. Its previous low was in 1980 when it won 33 percent.
Sikhs form the majority in Punjab, but constitute only two percent of India's population of 936 million. Hindus comprise 82 percent.

The BJP ruled India for 13 days following inconclusive national elections in May 1996, but failed to hold on to power when it could not muster a majority in the 545-seat Lok Sabha, or lower house of parliament.
